sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year, from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $216 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
Growth stalled at 0.2% in FY2023, then accelerated to 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025 [D284][D338][D393].
FY2024 growth came from Data Center revenue, which rose 217% to $47.5 billion [P23][S54].
FY2023 operating margin fell 21.6pp to 15.7% after $2.17 billion of inventory provisions hit gross margin [D299][F47][P35].
Data Center added 60.2pp of FY2026's 65.5% revenue growth and made up 89.7% of revenue [D622][D448][D620].
The filing attributes this to Data Center computing growth of 59% on Blackwell and networking growth of 142% on NVLink for GB200 and GB300 systems [P8].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Operating expenses rose 40.7% on employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs [D468][P9].
Diluted EPS compounded at 7.4% against net income at 60.8%, but share counts jumped in FY2022 and FY2025, so the EPS comparison looks unreliable [F216][F214][D251][D415].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 compares with a window median of 32.8%, a high of 62.4% and a low of 15.7% [F50][D813][D812][D811].
It slipped 2.0pp in FY2026: cost of revenue took 3.9pp, while R&D and SG&A added 1.3pp and 0.6pp [D463][D477][D478][D479].
FY2024's operating margin gained 38.5pp, led by cost of revenue at 15.8pp, R&D at 13.0pp and SG&A at 4.7pp [D353][D367][D368][D369].
The FY2024 gross margin gain reflected Data Center revenue growth of 217% and lower net inventory provisions as a share of revenue [P20].

Net margin of 55.6% sits below operating margin of 60.4%: tax rose to 15.1% on fewer tax benefits [F70][F50][D434][P2], while $11.1 billion of other income came from unrealized equity gains [X120][P3].
Operating cash flow of $103 billion was 0.86x net income, and free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin [F100][D435][F110][D432].
Free cash flow was 0.81x net income, the window low, against a semis peer median of 1.16x [D436][D826][D847].
Capex of $6.04 billion ran at 2.13x D&A, while inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%; the cited filings do not explain those builds [F105][D437][D474][D473].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion in FY2026 from $34.7 billion in FY2025 [D441][D386].
FY2026 cash and investments of $10.6 billion equal cash alone, so the 83rd percentile net cash rank among six semis peers is unreliable [D439][F150][D844].
Investing outflow rose to $52.2 billion, driven by equity investment purchases and a Groq license agreement [F120][P1].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion and dividends of $974 million used 42.5% of free cash flow, and diluted shares fell 1.2% [X150][X160][D444][D470].
Data quality: FY2026 net cash of $2.14 billion may omit investments, so no liquidity conclusion rests on it [D441][D439].
Concentration: one direct customer was 22% of FY2026 revenue and another was 14% [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% to $19.7 billion, cutting its share to 9.1% from 19.2%; the cited filings give no cause [D545][S24][D544][D541].
Inventory rose 112.3% to $21.4 billion, lifting days inventory to 125 days from 113 [D474][X222][D446][D391].
Candidate R1, the 25% Graphics fall in FY2023, is benign now because Graphics is 10.4% of revenue [R1][D754][D746].
Operating margin dropping below FY2024's 54.1%, rather than holding near FY2026's 60.4%, would reverse the margin story; check the FY2027 10-K [F48][F50].
Free cash flow to net income under the window low of 0.81x would confirm weakening conversion; check the FY2027 10-K [D826].
Days inventory above FY2026's 125 days would point to supply building ahead of demand; check the FY2027 10-K [D446].
